message.content: {"caption":"Two-panel line-and-bar chart comparing success rates across test-time scaling factors for three MaTTS configurations.","description":"The chart has panels for (a) Parallel Scaling and (b) Sequential Scaling. Both use scaling factor k=1–5 on the horizontal axis and Success Rate (SR) on a vertical axis running from 36 to 56. The shared legend identifies gray bars as “MaTTS w/o memory,” a blue dashed line with open diamond markers as “MaTTS w/o aggregation,” and a blue solid line with open circle markers as “MaTTS.” In parallel scaling, the gray bars rise from 39.0 to 42.2; the no-aggregation series is 49.7, 49.7, 51.3, 52.9, and 52.4, while MaTTS is 49.7, 50.3, 52.4, 54.0, and 55.1. The line series coincide at k=1; thereafter MaTTS rises more strongly, while no aggregation peaks at k=4 and dips at k=5. In sequential scaling, the gray bars are 39.0, 37.4, 38.5, 40.1, and 40.6; the no-aggregation series is 49.7, 50.8, 51.9, 52.4, and 51.9, while MaTTS is 49.7, 51.9, 53.5, 54.0, and 54.5.
